newsitem.title: USA: Calif. governor seeks extension on food stamps.
newsitem.headline: Calif. governor seeks extension on food stamps.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson on Thursday asked the federal government to allow the state to continue providing foods stamps to the poor through August 30.
Wilson, a Republican, submitted a request to the federal government to extend for six months California's waiver of the work requirement for able-bodied adults receiving food stamps.
"A number of counties have requested additional time to implement these changes, to notify food stamp recipients, and to help transition them into work programs," Wilson said.

"In response to these administrative concerns, I am submitting the waiver request to give counties the additional time they need to implement the new federal food stamp requirements," Wilson said in a statement.

Under the new federal welfare reform law, able-bodied people between the ages of 18 and 50 without children can receive food stamps for three months out of a three-year period unless they work part-time or participate in a welfare-to-work program.

California was previously granted a waiver from this requirement for 26 counties with unemployment rates higher than 10 percent. This new request would extend that waiver for six months to all 58 counties through August 30.
If the federal government approves the waiver request, counties that have cut off aid to recipients as of March 1 would be told to reinstate the food stamp benefits.
The expanded waiver request would affect an estimated 102,000 food stamp recipients, Wilson said.
